item.title: Galípolo diz ser normal que alta do crédito amplie endividamento, mas demonstra preocupação
item.description: O presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo, disse nesta segunda-feira ser normal que o endividamento no país cresça em meio a um cenário de impulso do crédito, mas demonstrou preocupação com o tema, citando crescimento de linhas de financiamento mais caras e sem garantia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo, disse nesta segunda-feira ser normal que o endividamento no país cresça em meio a um cenário de impulso do crédito, mas demonstrou preocupação com o tema, citando crescimento de linhas de financiamento mais caras e sem garantia. Em participação no evento Febraban Tech, em São Paulo, Galípolo afirmou que diante da ampliação do acesso a serviços financeiros no Brasil nos últimos anos, é importante promover o uso responsável dos instrumentos de crédito. Ele acrescentou que bancos precisam estar devidamente provisionados para o risco das operações que oferecem, ressaltando que o BC está debruçado sobre medidas prudenciais e avaliando experiências internacionais.

item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged allies on Monday to "do everything we can" and "dig into our own stocks of air defence" to protect Ukraine against Russian attacks at his first meeting co-chairing the so-called Coalition of the Willing.

item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged allies on Monday to "do everything we can" and "dig into our own stocks of air defence" to protect Ukraine against Russian attacks at [USN:L4N44K01O TEXT:"his first meeting"] co-chairing the so-called Coalition of the Willing. "(Russian President Vladimir) Putin is now hoping he can win through a campaign of terror using ballistic missiles against Ukrainian civilians ... This can never be the route to victory, and we need to be clear in sending that message," Burnham said at the start of the [USN:L8N44L0A5 TEXT:"meeting"]. "It means doing everything we can all do, and working with our allies as well, beyond this coalition, to dig into our own stocks of air defence ... to protect Ukraine from the missiles that are falling now." He also said there was a need for more sanctions on Russian oil and LNG exports to ramp up the pressure on Moscow.

item.title: FDA suspends licences of 5 food outlets at Mumbai Cricket Association site
item.description: The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids ...
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food licences of five outlets at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises over the alleged violation of food safety norms, flagging deficiencies in food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.As part of its statewide drive, the FDA has suspended licences of 11 food establishments, including the five outlets at MCA, it said on Monday.The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids, according to a press note.The five MCA outlets facing action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter. The FDA inspected the outlets on August 20 and found various deficiencies related to hygiene, food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.At the Permit Room, inspectors found ice accumulation in a kitchen refrigerator, an unclean and slippery floor near the kitchen entrance, inadequate temperature control, deteriorated raw material and deficiencies in food storage and handling.The outlet also lacked food-grade conformity certificates for food-contact packaging material and did not conduct regular checks of cooking oil.The Pavilion faced action after inspectors found ice accumulation and unclean refrigerator components, poor segregation of food items in cold storage, inadequate refrigeration calibration, improper thawing of frozen food and shortcomings in cooling and storage practices.At Mediterranean, the FDA found inadequate sanitisation of food equipment, improper cooling, poor portioning practices, inadequate thawing of frozen food, deficient temperature controls and shortcomings in the handling of raw materials and packaging.The Oriental Swing outlet was found to have an improperly calibrated refrigeration system, an unclean kitchen floor, damaged plaster or paint on part of the kitchen ceiling, inadequate sanitisation and deficiencies in temperature control and oil-quality checks.At the Clubway & Pastry Counter, the FDA found inadequate working space, improper storage of raw food, lack of hand gloves for a food handler and inadequate measures to prevent dust, dirt and insects from entering the food preparation area.It also found that the food business was being carried out under the name of an establishment that did not have a valid food licence. The registration certificate of the outlet was subsequently suspended, the release said.Besides the five MCA outlets, the statewide action included Lenexis Foodworks in Mahim, CafA Cadell in Shivaji Park, China Town Fast Food Centre in Mulund, Morya Misal in Warje and Saoji Upahar Gruh in Nagpur.The FDA suspended the registration of China Town Fast Food Centre with immediate effect after finding excessive use of artificial colour and MSG, repeated use of highly oxidised cooking oil, cockroach infestation, unhygienic food storage, a risk of cross-contamination between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and inadequate drainage.The FDA also suspended the licence of Morya Misal in Pune after finding artificial colouring in food, and storage and use of expired food products.The action comes as the FDA intensifies inspections of food establishments across Maharashtra to ensure compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.

item.title: Alibaba recua após venda de ações com grande desconto para investir em IA
item.description: As ações da gigante chinesa do comércio eletrônico Alibaba despencaram nesta segunda-feira, após a empresa ter lançado uma oferta de ações de US$10,2 bilhões com grande desconto para financiar investimento em inteligência artificial.
item.dc:creator: Kane Wu, Samuel Shen, Casey Hall
item.content:encoded: As ações da gigante chinesa do comércio eletrônico Alibaba (9988.HK) despencaram nesta segunda-feira, após a empresa ter lançado uma oferta de ações de US$10,2 bilhões com grande desconto para financiar investimento em inteligência artificial. A venda de ações do Alibaba é a maior oferta secundária de ações já realizada por uma empresa listada em Hong Kong e a terceira maior globalmente neste ano, atrás apenas das ofertas de quase US$85 bilhões da Alphabet (GOOGL.O) e de US$20 bilhões da Intel (INTC.O) . A companhia vendeu as ações com um desconto de 8,4% em relação ao fechamento de sexta-feira para levantar recursos para financiar chips, infraestrutura de IA e modelos. A IA se tornou o maior impulsionador do crescimento da receita do Alibaba em um momento em que o crescimento do comércio eletrônico está estagnado. Os modelos de IA do Alibaba estão entre os mais populares da China. Mesmo assim, alguns investidores têm reservas quanto ao sucesso dessa iniciativa. “O DNA do Alibaba está no comércio eletrônico, não na tecnologia avançada”, disse Yang Tingwu, vice-gerente geral da gestora de ativos Tongheng Investment. “Não importa o quanto invista em hardware de IA, provavelmente será superado pelos concorrentes em inovação tecnológica.” As ações do Alibaba chegaram a cair mais de 10%, mas reduziram as perdas e passaram a ser negociadas em linha com o desconto oferecido. A operação gerou forte demanda, atraindo US$ 28bilhões em ordens, incluindo US$6 bilhões de investidores de longo prazo e soberanos, segundo três fontes a par do assunto. Entre os investidores estão a Autoridade de Investimentos do Catar (QIA), o fundo soberano norueguês Norges e a Hillhouse, segundo uma das fontes. Representantes do Alibaba, Hillhouse, QIA e do Norges não comentaram. “A captação do Alibaba — ocorrido paralelamente a enormes operações da Alphabet e da Intel nos Estados Unidos — prova que os gigantes da tecnologia norte-americanos e chineses estão operando exatamente com o mesmo manual estratégico”, disse Winston Ma, professor adjunto da Faculdade de Direito da NYU e ex-diretor para a América do Norte do fundo soberano China Investment Corp. A oferta de ações ocorre uma semana depois que o Alibaba divulgou lucro líquido trimestral 75% menor em relação ao ano anterior, principalmente devido aos investimentos relacionados à IA. Reforçando como a IA passou a ser uma prioridade fundamental, o Alibaba separou este ano suas operações de IA de seu negócio de computação em nuvem, com a nova unidade a ser liderada pelo presidente-executivo, Eddie Wu. Além de se posicionar como um importante parceiro de IA para empresas que operam na China, a empresa está preparando a abertura de capital de sua divisão de fabricação de chips, a T-Head, e desenvolvendo agentes de IA que conectam serviços em todo o seu amplo ecossistema, incluindo compras, entrega de comida, viagens e entretenimento.

item.title: Tesoro de EEUU ampliará el alcance de las sanciones secundarias contra Irán: fuente
item.description: Se espera que el Tesoro de Estados Unidos amplíe el lunes el alcance de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que tengan lazos comerciales con Irán, en un momento en que la Administración Trump busca aumentar la presión económica sobre Teherán, informó una fuente a Reuters.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Se espera que el Tesoro de Estados Unidos amplíe el lunes el alcance de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que tengan lazos comerciales con Irán, en un momento en que la Administración Trump busca aumentar la presión económica sobre Teherán, informó una fuente a Reuters. La medida busca lanzar una última advertencia a los países para que rompan sus vínculos comerciales con Irán, en un intento por forzar el fin del conflicto de casi seis meses que ha bloqueado el estrecho de Ormuz y las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico, según la fuente, que pidió mantenerse en el anonimato al no estar autorizada a hablar en público sobre el asunto. Se espera que el secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, dé a conocer más detalles sobre las medidas contra Irán en una rueda de prensa a las 1700 GMT. La fuente indicó que Bessent también tiene la intención de ofrecer una visión general más amplia de la campaña de presión económica contra Irán que él y el presidente Donald Trump han descrito como un "Día D económico". Asimismo, dejará claro a los países que deben alinearse con Washington si no quieren arriesgarse a que sus principales empresas y entidades queden excluidas del sistema financiero basado en el dólar. La semana pasada, Bessent calificó las medidas contra Irán como las "sanciones más duras de la historia" y afirmó que, junto con el bloqueo naval estadounidense de los puertos iraníes, reducirían la necesidad de nuevas operaciones militares "cinéticas" contra Irán. Estados Unidos lleva décadas manteniendo sanciones contra Irán, en su mayoría para reducir sus ingresos petroleros, limitar el sector de la aviación, las criptomonedas, la adquisición de componentes de armas y otro material militar, así como cortar la financiación a las empresas controladas por el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica, una fuerza dominante en la economía iraní. Las sanciones excluyen a las entidades designadas del sistema financiero basado en el dólar, pero Teherán ha logrado crear rápidamente nuevas empresas pantalla, otras entidades y matrículas de buques para eludir las sanciones. La fuente afirmó que es probable que esta medida revele categorías adicionales de conductas relacionadas con Irán que podrían estar sujetas a sanciones secundarias en el futuro, lo que facilitaría la adopción de medidas contra quienes faciliten las transacciones en nombre del Gobierno iraní. La fuente no especificó las actividades que podrían estar sujetas a sanciones, pero señaló que, en el caso de determinados sectores iraníes, cualquier actividad, incluso en un tercer país, podría estar sujeta a sanciones secundarias. Actualmente, el Tesoro aprueba licencias para transacciones en varios sectores de Irán, entre ellos los de medicamentos y dispositivos médicos, los intercambios culturales y artísticos y las transacciones agrícolas. Un alto funcionario de la Administración afirmó que se espera que Bessent advierta de que deben cerrarse cualquier vía de financiación que aún quede abierta, incluso a través de bancos y terceros países que hayan tolerado determinadas actividades. El funcionario, que también habló bajo condición de anonimato, afirmó que el Tesoro "trazó un mapa de la red iraní de contrabando de petróleo y evasión de sanciones" y presentará esta información a los países que ayudan a Irán a eludir las sanciones a modo de advertencia. REPERCUSIÓN EN LAS RELACIONES CON CHINA En los últimos meses, el Tesoro ha sancionado a refinerías chinas independientes denominadas "teteras" por la compra de crudo iraní y ha ampliado sus medidas contra la flota clandestina de petroleros que transportan petróleo iraní. Una herramienta mucho más poderosa es la facultad de sancionar a bancos de China y otros países que facilitan transacciones con Irán, una medida que la Administración Trump no se ha mostrado dispuesta a adoptar hasta ahora, en medio de una delicada tregua comercial con Pekín. Como Trump y su par chino, Xi Jinping, tienen previsto reunirse en Washington a fines de septiembre, nuevas sanciones contra bancos chinos podrían empañar las perspectivas de prorrogar el acuerdo alcanzado en noviembre para mantener el flujo de tierras raras chinas y limitar los aranceles estadounidenses. El bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes ya ha frenado las ofertas chinas para comprar crudo iraní, según informó Reuters el viernes, lo que podría atenuar el impacto de las sanciones secundarias sobre China.

item.title: Italy's banking shake-up: all the M&A deals since 2025
item.description: Monte dei Paschi di Siena's simultaneous offers for Banco BPM and Banca Generali are the latest in a series of moves seeking to transform Italy's once-dormant banking sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Monte dei Paschi di Siena's (BMPS.MI) simultaneous offers for Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and Banca Generali (BGN.MI) are the latest in a series of moves seeking to transform Italy's once-dormant banking sector. The offers, unveiled last week as part of MPS' efforts to repel a hostile takeover by Italy's largest bank Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) , would create the country's third largest banking group. Here is a rundown of all the other completed and attempted Italian banking sector M&A deals since the start of 2025. 1. MONTE DEI PASCHI DI SIENA (MPS) - BANCO BPM - BANCA GENERALI MPS launched on August 21 separate [USN:L1N44H0NA TEXT:"all-share bids"] totalling about €34 billion ($40 billion) for rival Banco BPM and Generali-controlled (GASI.MI) wealth manager Banca Generali. CEO Luigi Lovaglio said MPS was the "natural partner for a friendly aggregation" and promised combined annual pre-tax synergies of around €2.6 billion. However, given Intesa's previously announced bid, under Italian takeover rules at least two thirds of MPS shareholders will have to clear the plan, in a vote scheduled for October 29. Previously, Banco BPM had invited MPS to discuss "[USN:L1N43X13W TEXT:"a merger of equals"]", but ended talks last month after France's Credit Agricole , its largest investor with a 29.3% stake, expressed its disapproval. 2. INTESA SANPAOLO - MONTE DEI PASCHI DI SIENA (MPS) - UNIPOL - BPER Intesa's unsolicited €30.6 billion [USN:L4N42G0DE TEXT:"cash-and-share bid"] for smaller rival MPS would create the euro zone's second-largest lender, placing Italy's top bank behind Spain's Banco Santander (SAN.MC) in terms of market value. Under the deal, Intesa would sell to Unipol (UNPI.MI) about half of the MPS retail network it would receive through the takeover. The network would then be combined with Unipol-backed lender BPER Banca (EMII.MI) to create a bank that would operate under the Monte dei Paschi brand. 3. UNICREDIT - COMMERZBANK UniCredit (CRDI.MI) , which stayed out of Italian M&A deals after a failed swoop on Banco BPM, said in July it had increased its stake in [USN:L8N43A0H6 TEXT:"Commerzbank"] (CBKG.DE) to 47.6%, pursuing a takeover bid despite German resistance. When excluding treasury shares, which carry no voting rights, UniCredit has a 49.7% voting stake in the German lender. It could further hike its stake by amending swap contracts. UniCredit, the second-largest bank in Italy, approached Commerzbank about merger talks [USN:S8N3J3082 TEXT:"as early as September 2024"], after it bought a 9% in the German peer and signalled it was open to taking more. 4. CF+ - BANCA SISTEMA Elliott-backed speciality lender Banca CF+ completed in March a €145-million offer for rival Banca Sistema (BSTA.MI) . 5. MPS - MEDIOBANCA In September last year, MPS completed a €16-billion takeover of merchant bank Mediobanca, thus also becoming the main investor in insurer Generali, a coveted asset in Italian finance. The deal, coming from a bank bailed out by the government in 2017 and reprivatised in 2023-2024, turned MPS into a [USN:L2N3V90Q0 TEXT:"key M&A actor"]. 6. BANCA IFIS - ILLIMITY Venice-based IFIS (IF.MI) completed in August 2025 a €298-million cash-and-shares offer for Illimity, a digital bank founded by former industry minister and veteran banker Corrado Passera, which was later delisted from the Milan bourse. 7. BPER - BANCA POPOLARE DI SONDRIO Italy's fourth-largest bank in July 2025 completed a €5.4 billion cash-and-share offer for the smaller peer based in the northern city of Sondrio, calling it a defensive move dictated by the accelerating consolidation. Insurer Unipol, the main shareholder in both banks, played a pivotal role. 8. UNICREDIT - BANCO BPM Italy's second-biggest bank [USN:L8N3TJ0Y1 TEXT:"dropped"] its €15-billion all-share offer for Banco BPM in July 2025, blaming conditions the government had set to clear the deal. UniCredit had presented its bid in November 2024. 9. BANCO BPM - ANIMA HOLDING Shortly before UniCredit's failed takeover gambit, Banco BPM had bid to buy fund manager Anima Holding (ANIM.MI) , a €1.8 billion-euro acquisition it [USN:S8N3OK0C7 TEXT:"completed in April 2025"]. 10. MEDIOBANCA - BANCA GENERALI In an [USN:L8N3UD0BK TEXT:"unsuccessful attempt"] to thwart MPS' takeover bid, Mediobanca announced in April 2025 a €6.3-billion all-share offer for wealth manager Banca Generali (BGN.MI) . It failed to win shareholders' approval for it. 11. BANCA GENERALI - INTERMONTE Banca Generali completed in January 2025 a €98.2 million euro purchase of broker Intermonte, to boost its investment banking skills and complement its wealth management offer with corporate finance advisory services. ($1 = 0.8574 euros)

item.title: From Tokyo to London, heatwaves send men to work in shorts
item.description: Scorching summer temperatures have done what decades of dress-down Fridays have failed to do — get men to the office in shorts.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka Olenska, Helen Reid, James Davey
item.content:encoded: Scorching summer temperatures have done what decades of dress-down Fridays have failed to do — get men to the office in shorts. Japan's capital led the way. This year the metropolitan government's long-standing no-tie, no-jacket [USN:L6N43H0CH TEXT:""Cool Biz""] campaign took a step further by encouraging its staff to ditch long trousers, and even try T-shirts and sneakers. As [USN:L8N44G0YD TEXT:"heatwaves mounted"] across Europe, other workers followed in Tokyo's wake, sometimes with the encouragement of authorities and management, sometimes without. LINE BETWEEN COMMUTER AND HOLIDAY STYLES BLURRING Major retailers told Reuters linen shorts and suits were flying off the shelves in Britain, as men opted for breathable fabrics more commonly associated with Mediterranean climes. "The lines between 'commuter' and 'holiday' style are blurring," Martha Hibberd, menswear buyer at British department store John Lewis, said. Marks and Spencer (MKS.L) said sales of men's linen trousers in June to July jumped 183% compared with the same period a year ago. H&M (HMb.ST) — one of Europe's biggest fashion retailers — said it was bringing in lighter clothes and delaying the release of autumnal lines to later in the year. "It looks like we're not going back when it comes to climate change," Andreas Lowenstam, H&M's head of menswear design, said. Hugo Boss said it has increased its assortment of tailored shorts. Its "Boss by Beckham" range in collaboration with soccer star David Beckham, offers a pair of cotton tailored shorts for €229 ($267.27). 'SHORTS ARE FOR WEEKENDS' The trend was there to see in Europe's business hubs, from London's Canary Wharf to the streets of Frankfurt. But there were some limits. At Norway's largest bank, DNB, staff were welcome to wear shorts and skirts, spokesperson Vidar Korsberg Dalsbo told Reuters. "However, we are probably talking about smarter garments with some length rather than a ballerina skirt or a cheeky pair of 1970s-style soccer shorts." In June, Gianfranco Lot, Switzerland head at insurance group Swiss Re (SRENH.S) , wrote an email to staff with tips on how to stay cool. Alongside the list of suggestions — such as drinking water, breaking when needed, and taking a dip in Lake Zurich just across from the office — there was a quick reminder that "shorts are for weekends". Pushing back against the traditions, there were signs that some workers were prepared to take a stand for their lighter attire. Germany's biggest union, IG Metall, and services sector union Verdi both told Reuters they believed dress codes should be relaxed or waived if necessary at times of higher temperatures. "Summers are getting hotter, heat waves are becoming more frequent, and the strain on workers is noticeably increasing," Moriz Tiedemann, occupational health expert at IG Metall, said. Some were already taking matters into their own hands. In Warsaw, one bus driver decided he had had enough of the standard uniform of long polyester trousers and turned up to work one day this month in a skirt, as a protest. "These materials make us sweat and overheat," said the man, who only gave his name as Darek. At the last count, a petition launched by one of his colleagues, asking the Polish capital's transport authority ZTM to let drivers wear shorts during hot weather, had collected more than 400 signatures. ($1 = 0.8568 euros)

item.title: Trump amenaza arancel del 50% a todos los autos y camiones en disputa comercial con Canadá
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró en una publicación en redes sociales el lunes que los aranceles a todos los autos y camiones, las autopartes y el acero se incrementarán al 50% a partir del 1 de enero de 2027, tras el fracaso de las negociaciones comerciales con Canadá.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró en una publicación en redes sociales el lunes que los aranceles a todos los autos y camiones, las autopartes y el acero se incrementarán al 50% a partir del 1 de enero de 2027, tras el fracaso de las negociaciones comerciales con Canadá. "Si se fabrica en Estados Unidos, los aranceles son CERO. ¡Canadá ya no recibirá el mismo trato que un estado!", escribió Trump. "En materia de comercio, y también en otros aspectos, se encuentran entre las peores naciones del mundo con las que tratar. Se creen con derecho a todo y, sin embargo, ¡NOSOTROS NO NECESITAMOS A CANADÁ, SON ELLOS LOS QUE NOS NECESITAN!", agregó. La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios en la que se pidieron más detalles sobre los aranceles con los que se había amenazado. Los representantes del Gobierno canadiense tampoco respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Los dos países no lograron alcanzar un acuerdo comercial el viernes y cada parte culpó a la otra. Canadá está preparando aranceles sobre algunos productos estadounidenses en represalia por los gravámenes del 50% impuestos por Trump a otros bienes. Los principales fabricantes de automóviles no se pronunciaron de inmediato sobre el anuncio de Trump. Sin embargo, algunos ejecutivos del sector, que hablaron con Reuters bajo condición de anonimato, se mostraron escépticos, señalando que Trump ya anunció antes aranceles elevados que nunca se materializaron y que cualquier gravamen de esa magnitud probablemente provocaría una represalia masiva por parte de Canadá. También señalaron que aún faltarán meses varios meses hasta enero tras las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre y que la amenaza de Trump podría tener como objetivo reanudar las negociaciones.

item.title: 英国、ウクライナにミサイル部品の機密開示へ－防空能力強化を支援
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国のバーナム首相は24日、ウクライナを訪問し、ゼレンスキー大統領への支持を示すとともに、冬を前にウクライナの防空能力強化を支援する方針を表明した。同氏は、長距離巡航ミサイル「スカルプ」に使われる英国製部品に関する機密情報について、英防衛企業MBDAによる開示を認めると発表した。

バーナム氏はウクライナによるロシアへの抵抗を、第2次世界大戦での英国のナチス・ドイツとの戦いになぞらえ、結束を強調した。7月の首相就任以来、バーナム氏は国内政策を優先してきたが、国際舞台での指導力も強調したい考えだ。

ウクライナ独立35周年を記念し、キーウの聖ソフィア大聖堂前で行った演説で、バーナム氏は「ウクライナ国民の圧倒的な強さには、心から畏敬の念を抱く」と述べ、「20世紀にはわが国が欧州の自由の炎を守り続けた。21世紀にはあなた方がその炎を守っている。ロシアはわが国に言語道断の脅しをかけているが、われわれはウクライナへの支援を続ける」と呼びかけた。

バーナム氏は同日、ゼレンスキー氏と「有志連合」による会合も共同主催した。ドイツのメルツ首相やフランスのマクロン大統領がオンライン参加したとみられる。

スカルプは、英国の長距離巡航ミサイル「ストームシャドー」のフランス製造版で、両ミサイルには英仏共通の技術が使われている。情報開示により、フランスとウクライナは早ければ今年末にも、ウクライナ国内でスカルプを組み立てられるようになる。

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官は24日、スカルプに使われる英国製部品の機密情報開示の計画について、ロシア政府は「極めて否定的」に受け止めていると記者団に述べた。ペスコフ氏は「英国はウクライナ政府側に立ってこの戦争に参加し、組織的かつ継続的に火に油を注ぎ、和平プロセスのいかなる進展も阻止しようと策を巡らせている」と語った。

同氏は、ロシア軍がこうしたミサイルの生産拠点の特定を進めており、「関連施設を破壊するための措置を講じている」としている。

item.title: Tech stocks today: All eyes on Nvidia as Meta trial resumes
item.description: This week's major tech news
item.dc:creator: Daniel Howley

LIVE Updated 43 mins ago

It's nearly here. The moment Wall Street waits for every quarter since the AI trade kicked off: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) second quarter earnings. Yes, while its Big Tech peers reported their results nearly a month ago, Nvidia is finally giving us the lowdown on its latest quarter when it reports Q2 earnings after the close on Wednesday. For the quarter, Nvidia is expected to report second quarter adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $92 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. That would mark a 96% year-over-year jump in overall revenue, and a continued quarter-over-quarter acceleration. ( NVDA ) Go deeper with AlphaSpace

209.84 -4.88 (-2.28%) As of 10:44:42 AM EDT. Market Open.

And Meta's social media addiction trial resumes in Oakland, Calif., today after Thursday's hearing was postponed due to a sick juror. A collection of 29 state attorneys general is suing the social media giant over claims that it purposely developed its services to keep children online as long as possible and caused psychological harm. The trial is a test case for that larger suit and involves the attorneys general from four states. Meta claims the trial could leave it exposed to as much as $1.4 trillion in damages, but state attorneys general dispute that figure.

item.title: Red-hot Phillies take 'fighting' spirit out west to face Mariners
item.description: It sounds corny, but the Philadelphia Phillies seem to have found their mojo in an unlikely spot.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: It sounds corny, but the Philadelphia Phillies seem to have found their mojo in an unlikely spot. The Phillies have won nine games in a row, sparked by a 7-1 victory against Minnesota in MLB's Field of Dreams game Aug. 13 in Dyersville, Iowa, when Kyle Schwarber hit two home runs into the stalk yard. The winning streak continued for the Phillies on Sunday when they rallied from a four-run deficit with two outs in the bottom of the ninth inning, defeating St. Louis 6-4 on Schwarber's tiebreaking, two-run blast. The Phillies will try to extend their streak to double digits when they open a three-game interleague series Monday night against the host Seattle Mariners. "You can talk about the resilience, the no quit, and that's why you play all the outs," said Schwarber, who leads the majors with 39 home runs. "You're in it until you're not." Edmundo Sosa's two-strike double with the bases loaded trimmed St. Louis' lead to 4-3 on Sunday. Bryan De La Cruz singled to tie the score, also with two strikes, to set the stage for Schwarber's 459-foot blast to straightaway center field. "We're the Phillies; I can't say I'm really surprised," Sosa said through a translator. "When we're late in the game, we never stop fighting. It's just a magical day." The Phillies have a four-game cushion in the National League's wild-card race and are within three games of first-place Atlanta in the NL East. "It's a lot of complete baseball," Schwarber said. "It's not like we're out there just hitting homers and relying on that. I feel like there's a lot of different things that we're doing well. I feel like the defense is playing really well. Our pitching, obviously, is our pitching; our starters set the tone for us." The Mariners had won five of their past seven games in their effort to track down an American League playoff berth before being blown out 19-2 Sunday by the visiting Chicago Cubs. The Mariners' Randy Arozarena went deep leading off for a second straight game to clinch a sixth successive season with at least 20 homers and 20 steals, but that was Seattle's lone highlight. With a short-handed bullpen, the Mariners had to use left-handed reliever Jose A. Ferrer for 1 2/3 innings, which could prove costly against left-handed Phillies sluggers Schwarber and Bryce Harper in the coming days. "It was the situation that we had at hand and, just, it ended up, you know, not going our way," said Mariners manager Dan Wilson, who used a pair of position players to mop up. "It made it difficult there at the end." Monday's series opener will feature a pair of former All-Star right-handers in the Phillies' Zack Wheeler (10-4, 2.92 ERA) and the Mariners' Logan Gilbert (10-7, 3.35). Wheeler has dropped his past three decisions, though he didn't get one Tuesday in a 6-4 victory against visiting Miami when he allowed two runs on two hits over five innings, with four walks and seven strikeouts. He's 1-0 with an 0.00 ERA in one previous start against Seattle. Gilbert has won his past two starts. He won 7-5 Wednesday at Milwaukee, giving up three runs on four hits over five innings, with four walks and five strikeouts. He's 0-3 with a 7.50 ERA in four career starts against the Phillies. --Field Level Media

item.title: Veneza inclui documentário sobre Gaza, dirigido por vencedores do Oscar, na competição principal
item.description: Um documentário que aborda a morte de civis em Gaza pelas forças israelenses foi incluído na programação do Festival de Cinema de Veneza nesta segunda-feira, sendo este o segundo ano consecutivo em que uma obra polêmica sobre o conflito concorre ao prestigioso Leão de Ouro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Um documentário que aborda a morte de civis em Gaza pelas forças israelenses foi incluído na programação do Festival de Cinema de Veneza nesta segunda-feira, sendo este o segundo ano consecutivo em que uma obra polêmica sobre o conflito concorre ao prestigioso Leão de Ouro. Os organizadores do festival informaram que “NAZA”, dirigido pela dupla israelense Yuval Abraham e Rachel Szor, fará parte da programação principal do evento, que acontecerá de 2 a 12 de setembro — sendo o único documentário entre os 21 concorrentes deste ano. No ano passado, “A Voz de Hind Rajab”, que conta a história angustiante das últimas horas de uma menina de Gaza presa em um carro sob fogo israelense, conquistou o segundo prêmio em Veneza após receber uma ovação de pé recorde de 23 minutos em sua estreia. De acordo com uma sinopse divulgada pelo festival, “NAZA” foi filmado à noite nos telhados de Tel Aviv e “revela em detalhes os mecanismos por trás do extermínio em massa calculado de civis palestinos em Gaza por parte de Israel”. Autoridades de saúde palestinas afirmam que mais de 73 mil pessoas foram mortas em Gaza depois que Israel lançou sua campanha militar contra o enclave costeiro em outubro de 2023, na sequência do ataque do Hamas a Israel, que matou cerca de 1.200 pessoas, segundo dados israelenses. O Ministério da Saúde de Gaza não faz distinção entre civis e combatentes em sua contagem. Israel afirma que sua ofensiva tinha como alvo o Hamas e que tentou evitar a morte de civis, mas que o grupo se escondia entre a população civil — uma alegação que o Hamas nega. Abraham e Szor foram dois dos quatro codiretores de “Sem Chão”, que ganhou o Oscar de melhor documentário em 2025. O filme narrava a destruição de uma comunidade palestina na Cisjordânia ocupada por Israel e a expansão implacável dos assentamentos judeus. “NAZA” foi produzido pelo jornal britânico The Guardian e por James Wilson, com produção executiva de Jonathan Glazer, diretor vencedor do Oscar pelo drama sobre o Holocausto de 2023 “Zona de Interesse”. Wilson e Glazer também foram, respectivamente, produtor e produtor executivo de “A Voz de Hind Rajab”. Na semana passada, as autoridades israelenses abriram uma investigação criminal sobre a morte da menina. “NAZA” estreará em Veneza no dia 10 de setembro. O filme se junta a uma seletiva lista que inclui novos trabalhos de Martin McDonagh, Florian Zeller, Danny Boyle, Werner Herzog e Hirokazu Kore-eda.

item.title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on all cars and trucks amid Canada trade spat
item.description: U.S. tariffs on all cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel will be increased to 50% starting January 1, 2027, President Donald Trump said in a social post on Monday after trade talks with Canada collapsed over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: U.S. tariffs on all cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel will be increased to 50% starting January 1, 2027, President Donald Trump said in a social post on Monday after trade [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"talks with Canada collapsed"] over the weekend. "Build in the U.S. and there are ZERO TARIFFS. Canada will be treated like a State no longer!" Trump wrote. "On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with. They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!" The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment seeking more details on the threatened tariffs. Representatives for the Canadian government also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The two countries failed to reach a trade deal late on Friday, with each side blaming the other as Canada readied tariffs on some U.S. goods in retaliation for 50% levies ordered by Trump on other Canadian products. Major automakers did not immediately comment on Trump's announcement. But auto executives, speaking to Reuters on the condition of anonymity, raised skepticism about Trump's threat, noting the president has previously announced large tariffs that never materialized and that any tariff of that size would likely spark a massive Canadian retaliation. They also noted January was months away following November's midterm elections and that Trump's threat could aimed at restarting talks.

item.title: Wall Street drifts ahead of a big week that could swing stocks and bonds
item.description: World shares were mostly lower and oil prices slipped on Monday at the outset of a week capped by an annual meeting of top U.S. economic officials at Jackson Hole, Wyoming.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — U.S. stocks are drifting Monday ahead of a week packed with potentially market-moving events. The areas of the bond market that the U.S. Treasury Department is trying to calm down, meanwhile, eased a bit. The S&P 500 slipped 0.3 per cent and pulled a bit further from its all-time high set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 49 points, or 0.1 per cent, as of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.6 per cent lower. Tech stocks led the way downward following big swings through the summer on worries that the frenzy around artificial-intelligence technology sent prices too high and that the huge demand for AI chips won’t be sustainable if they don’t produce enough profits. Chip giant Nvidia has been a tremendous winner of the AI boom and become Wall Street’s largest and most influential stock because of it. It will deliver its latest quarterly earnings report on Wednesday, which could dictate the next big move for AI-related stocks. Nvidia slipped 0.7 per cent and was one of the heaviest weights on the S&P 500, where the majority of stocks were rising. Drops of 5.5 per cent for Micron Technology and 1.5 per cent for Broadcom also helped drag the index lower. The other big factor moving stocks recently has been the bond market, where longer-term Treasury yields climbed through the summer on worries about high inflation, huge government debts and other factors. High yields make it more expensive for everyone to borrow, not just the government, and have already been pushing up mortgage rates and hurting the housing industry. The U.S. Treasury Department announced a surprise move last week to increase the size of planned buybacks of Treasurys, which could help ease the rise in yields for 10- and 30-year Treasurys. But analysts warned the move could have only a limited effect because of how small the size of the buybacks are and how they do not fix the fundamental problems of too-high debt for the U.S. government and expensive oil prices because of the war with Iran. On Monday, the yield of the 10-year Treasury eased to 4.70 per cent from 4.74 per cent late Friday and is back below where it was late Tuesday, before the U.S. Treasury Department made its surprise announcement. Analysts warn the U.S. government’s attempts to push longer-term yields downward could ultimately mean higher pressure on inflation. Inflation already is higher than nearly everyone would like and has been for years. That raises the pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise the federal funds rate that it controls, which affects very short-term overnight loans. When the Fed raises that rate, it can help keep a lid on inflation by trying to slow the overall economy and undercutting prices for stocks and other investments. The Fed’s new chairman, Kevin Warsh, is set to deliver a speech on Friday at an economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. The mountain setting has provided the backdrop for major Fed policy announcements in the past, but investors are unsure of what they may get from Warsh this time around. Warsh has insisted that he wants to give financial markets fewer clues about what the Fed will do with interest rates, hoping that markets react more to incoming data about the economy and inflation than to what the Fed is signaling. Helping to curb some of the worries on inflation Monday was a drop in oil prices. Brent crude fell 1.3 per cent to US$91.51 per barrel. Last month it zigzagged between US$72 and US$102 as hopes rose and fell that the United States and Iran could reach a deal that would allow oil tankers to freely exit the Persian Gulf again. In stock markets abroad, indexes dipped around much of the world. South Korea’s Kospi fell 3.1 per cent, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 1.9 per cent for two of the biggest moves. Seoul has been home to some of the world’s sharpest swings this summer because it is dominated by two tech titans benefiting from the AI boom, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writers Michelle Chapman and Elaine Kurtenbach contributed to this report.

item.title: Govt appoints ex-diplomat Akbaruddin, two others to RBI central board
item.description: The central government has appointed former diplomat Syed Akbaruddin, ex-bureaucrat Annie George Mathew, and consultancy BCG India Chairman Janmejaya Kumar Sinha to RBI central board.
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: The central government has appointed former diplomat Syed Akbaruddin, ex-bureaucrat Annie George Mathew, and consultancy BCG India Chairman Janmejaya Kumar Sinha to RBI central board.They have been appointed as part-time, Non-official Directors on the Central Board of Reserve Bank of India for four years with effect from August 24 or until further orders, whichever is earlier, the central bank said in a release on Monday.Last week, the government had re-appointed industrialist Anand Gopal Mahindra as part-time, Non-official Director on the board.Former ISRO Chairman Somanath Sreedhara Panicker was also appointed on the board last week.Other members of the board include Revathy Iyer, a retired officer from the Indian Audit & Accounts Service, who went on to become the Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General, Government Accounts, and Sachin Chaturvedi, Director General of think tank Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS).Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governors Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, SC Murmu and Rohit Jain, economic affairs secretary Anuradha Thakur and financial services secretary Sanjay Lohia are also on the board.

item.title: UK police arrest 12 after linking crash that killed seven to organised crime
item.description: British police investigating a car crash in northeast England over the weekend that killed seven people, including two police officers, said on Monday they had arrested 12 people in a probe into organised criminal activity linked to the incident.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British police investigating a car crash in northeast England over the weekend that killed [USN:L1N44J02B TEXT:"seven people"], including two police officers, said on Monday they had arrested 12 people in a probe into organised criminal activity linked to the incident. Cleveland Police said officers had received reports before the crash on Saturday of two cars being driven dangerously, including a vehicle that was seen ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area. Both vehicles had been operating with cloned number plates to avoid detection, police said. One of the vehicles drove the wrong way down a major road and crashed into a police armed response car, killing all five occupants and two police officers. Four of the five occupants of the vehicle that crashed had previous convictions, police said. Police said inquiries over the weekend had resulted in the arrests of nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, across the Teesside area. The suspects were arrested on suspicion of offences ranging from possession of a firearm to participating in the activities of an organised crime group, police said. "This has been a fast-moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity," Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said in a statement. Police added there was currently no evidence that the events leading up to the crash had been filmed to appear on short-form video platform TikTok, after recent concerns in [USN:L1N44E07O TEXT:"neighbouring Ireland"] about motorists driving the wrong way on roads for social media attention.

item.title: L'Ukraine veut la paix, mais ne se soumettra pas, dit Zelensky
item.description: L'Ukraine veut la paix mais elle ne se soumettra jamais à la Russie, a déclaré lundi le président Volodimir Zelensky dans un discours pugnace prononcé à l'occasion du 35e anniversaire de l'Indépendance de son pays.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Anna Pruchnicka
item.content:encoded: L'Ukraine veut la paix mais elle ne se soumettra jamais à la Russie, a déclaré lundi le président Volodimir Zelensky dans un discours pugnace prononcé à l'occasion du 35e anniversaire de l'Indépendance de son pays. Flanqué du Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham et du président du Conseil européen, Antonio Costa, le président ukrainien a salué la résilience de son peuple après plus de quatre années de guerre. "L'Ukraine veut absolument la paix, mais elle n'est pas prête à capituler", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky, se disant convaincu que Moscou ne mettrait pas fin à sa guerre d'invasion si Kyiv acceptait de lui céder davantage de territoires dans l'est du pays, une des conditions posées par Vladimir Poutine pour mettre fin au conflit. Vêtu d'une chemise traditionnelle brodée, le dirigeant ukrainien a remercié les dirigeants étrangers qui se sont déplacés à Kyiv pour afficher leur soutien, malgré la menace constante d'attaques de missiles russes, l'Ukraine étant confrontée à une pénurie de moyens de défense antiaérienne américains. Le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham, qui a pris ses fonctions le mois dernier, a déclaré que son choix de se rendre à Kyiv pour son premier déplacement à l'étranger témoignait de l'importance qu'il accorde à l'Ukraine. "Nous serons à vos côtés dans ce combat jusqu'au bout, de tout notre coeur et de toute notre âme", a-t-il dit, réitérant son soutien "malgré les menaces scandaleuses de la Russie à l'encontre de mon pays". La Grande-Bretagne a annoncé lundi qu'elle autoriserait Kyiv à accéder à une technologie jusqu'ici classifiée afin de lancer la production de missiles de croisière franco-britanniques à longue portée de type SCALP, capables de mener des frappes en profondeur sur le territoire russe. Réagissant à cette annonce, le Kremlin a accusé Londres de "jeter de l'huile sur le feu", après avoir déjà dit la semaine dernière que la livraison de drones britanniques à l'Ukraine aurait "des conséquences". Andy Burnham devait coprésider lundi une réunion virtuelle de la "Coalition des volontaires" avec le président français Emmanuel Macron et le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz. Les dirigeants européens devaient discuter de la demande de Volodimir Zelensky visant à obtenir davantage de systèmes de défense antiaérienne afin d'empêcher les missiles balistiques russes de pilonner les villes ukrainiennes, les stocks de missiles intercepteurs Patriot américains ayant été épuisés par la guerre entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Le président ukrainien a déclaré samedi que l'effort de guerre de Kyiv était compliqué par un déficit de financement de 27 milliards de dollars cette année. Il a également averti que la Russie pourrait opter pour une nouvelle escalade en se préparant à mobiliser quelque 300.000 soldats supplémentaires après les élections législatives du mois prochain. Rendant hommage au peuple ukrainien et aux soldats qui défendent l'Ukraine, Volodimir Zelensky a appelé les alliés à lui fournir "tout" ce qui est nécessaire pour mettre fin au conflit. "Nous ne vous demandons pas de vous battre à notre place", a-t-il répété.

item.title: India faces weakest monsoon in nearly two decades as El Nino strengthens
item.description: India is on course for its weakest monsoon in nearly two decades, with rainfall likely to end the season around 15% below the long-term average, the lowest since 2009, two senior weather department sources said.
item.dc:creator: Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: India is on course for its weakest monsoon in nearly two decades, with rainfall likely to end the season around 15% below the long-term average, the lowest since 2009, two senior weather department sources said. The weak monsoon could hurt crop output, drive up food prices and curb rural incomes in the world's fifth-largest economy, where the rains provide around 70% of the country's annual rainfall. A lack of good rains in the crucial crop-maturing month of September could dent yields of summer-sown crops such as cotton, soybean, corn and pulses, while also depleting soil moisture needed for winter-sown crops such as wheat and rapeseed. "We are witnessing the impact of El Nino on monsoon rainfall. It is likely to be severe in September, and we could see a double-digit deficit in rainfall," said a senior official with the India Meteorological Department (IMD), who declined to be named as he was not authorised to speak with media. India could receive 15% below-average rainfall, or 85% of normal, during the June-September season, which would be the lowest rainfall since 2009, he said. That would be nearly double the 8% deficit projected in the weather department's [USN:L1N40W0BS TEXT:"initial forecast"]. Except for some eastern states, most parts of the country are likely to receive below-average rainfall in September, widening the seasonal deficit, he added. The IMD is expected to issue its official forecast for September at the end of this month. The monsoon this year could begin withdrawing from northwestern parts of the country a few days earlier than usual next month, unless a fresh weather system develops, said a second weather department source, who did not want to be identified in line with official rules. The monsoon typically begins in June and starts to retreat by September 17 from northwestern parts of the country, ending across the country by mid-October. El Nino is strengthening and is likely to intensify further in September, suppressing rainfall over India, they said. A climate pattern marked by unusually warm sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, El Nino disrupts global weather patterns and can bring drier conditions to parts of Southeast Asia and other regions. In the past, India has experienced below-average rainfall during most El Nino years, sometimes leading to severe droughts that destroyed crops and forced authorities to limit the export of some grains. India has received 13% less rainfall than average since the monsoon season began on June 1. Rainfall was 35.4% below average in June before a 1% surplus in July offered a brief reprieve. The monsoon weakened again in August, with rainfall so far running 15% below average.

item.title: H.B. Fuller rejects Ancora's $1.2 billion bid for adhesive unit
item.description: H.B. Fuller said on Monday its board unanimously rejected activist investor Ancora's unsolicited proposal to acquire its Building Adhesives Solutions (BAS) business, arguing that the offer significantly undervalued the unit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: H.B. Fuller (FUL.N) said on Monday its board unanimously rejected activist investor Ancora's unsolicited proposal to acquire its Building Adhesives Solutions (BAS) business, arguing that the offer significantly undervalued the unit. In a letter to Ancora, H.B. Fuller said the proposal ignored the unit's growth prospects and lacked key details regarding Ancora's ability to execute the deal. "As key construction end markets recover and benefit from tailwinds such as the data center buildout, we expect BAS to be a significant driver of earnings moving forward," said H.B. Fuller's board chair, Teresa Rasmussen. Earlier this month, Ancora had [USN:L4N449146 TEXT:"proposed to buy"] Fuller's unit for as much as $1.2 billion in cash. Rasmussen added that carving out the BAS business would result in material operating inefficiencies as it shares manufacturing infrastructure with the company's other businesses. A surge in dealmaking activity has fueled campaigns by activist investors, who push companies to sell their entire business or parts of it, putting boards and management teams under greater pressure. "By rejecting the offer without any engagement, CEO Celeste Mastin and the board have reinforced their proclivity for entrenchment," Ancora's President Jim Chadwick told Reuters. Chadwick added that Ancora could self-finance a transaction, increase its offer and move quickly to address the company's leverage crisis. Ancora also criticized H.B. Fuller's response to the bid, saying it strengthened its case for board changes and claimed there was interest in both the BAS segment and the entire company from other parties.

item.title: US FDA extends review of Capricor's muscle disorder therapy by three months
item.description: Capricor Therapeutics said on Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review of its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR.O) said on Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review of its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months. Shares of the company surged over 20% in early morning trading, as the update boosted market sentiment after a setback last month when an FDA advisory panel [USN:L4N43V2DJ TEXT:"voted"] nine-to-three against the effectiveness data of the drug. The health regulator set the deadline to November 22 to allow more time to review new clinical trial data submitted by the company. Capricor's therapy, called deramiocel, aims to treat Duchenne, a rare and progressive genetic disease that causes muscle wasting and mostly affects boys. "With an additional year of follow-up from HOPE-3, we now have one of the most extensive clinical datasets evaluating upper limb function in Duchenne," said Capricor CEO Linda Marbán.

item.title: Veteran pitchers square off for Cubs, D-backs in wild-card chase
item.description: The Chicago Cubs will look to bolster their shrinking National League wild-card lead against an Arizona Diamondbacks team striving to remain in the playoff race when the teams open a three-game series in Phoenix on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Cubs will look to bolster their shrinking National League wild-card lead against an Arizona Diamondbacks team striving to remain in the playoff race when the teams open a three-game series in Phoenix on Monday night. The Cubs will turn to newcomer Kevin Gausman (6-11, 4.58 ERA) to try to turn things around after a 10-game stretch that has seen their lead for the NL's top wild-card spot dwindle from 6 1/2 games to two. The Cubs (75-56) are 4-6 over the past 10 games after salvaging the final game of a three-game set in Seattle with a 19-2 rout on Sunday that included MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong's 33rd home run and 32nd stolen base of the season. "That's a good finishing game for a series," said Cubs reliever Aaron Civale, who threw four scoreless innings of one-hit ball for the win. "Continue to ride that momentum into the next series." With a 9-1 run over the past 10 games, the Philadelphia Phillies moved into the second NL wild-card spot, just two games behind the Cubs. The Phillies (73-58) and Cubs have an edge over the San Diego Padres (71-60) and Diamondbacks (69-62) as the four fight for the league's three wild-card spots. Arizona veteran right-hander Merrill Kelly (8-11, 5.37 ERA) will look to halt a personal two-game losing streak on Monday. The 35-year-old Gausman, meanwhile, will make his fourth start for the Cubs since being obtained from the Toronto Blue Jays this month. He won his first Cubs' appearance on Aug. 7, throwing seven innings in a quality start in a 6-4 victory at Kansas City, but he has struggled since. Gausman dealt with cramping of his left thumb last Tuesday against the Chicago White Sox in his most recent outing. The Cubs won 4-3, but Gausman came out of the game in the fifth inning and didn't figure into the decision. "I just felt like I couldn't keep going," he said after the game. "I kind of couldn't grab my glove without it locking up on me. It's pretty frustrating, to be honest. First start here (Wrigley Field) as a Cub. Obviously not what I'm trying to do." Gausman is 1-1 with a 6.19 ERA in his first three Cubs' starts, with 16 strikeouts and four walks in 16 innings. The Nationals got to him for six runs in 4 2/3 innings of a 7-0 Cubs loss at Washington on Aug. 13. Gausman is 7-2 with a 3.20 ERA in 11 appearances (10 starts) against Arizona. Kelly knows all about cramping, with leg cramps having forced him out of a half-dozen games in the last four seasons. He has struggled since being removed in the sixth inning of Arizona's 4-3 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Aug. 7 because of a right leg cramp. Kelly is 0-3 with one no-decision in four August starts. He has given up 18 runs on 23 hits, including four home runs, in 19 2/3 innings this month and has an 8.24 ERA. Kelly is 3-2 with a 4.07 ERA in nine career starts against the Cubs. He was the losing pitcher in an 8-4 Chicago victory on May 3 after allowing six runs on eight hits and three walks in 4 1/3 innings. But the Diamondbacks are looking forward to September. "I think we can be really good (down the final stretch)," veteran infielder Nolan Arenado said. "There's still some things we can be better at. Our pitching and our bullpen has been phenomenal. Our defense is phenomenal. "It sounds crazy, but I still feel like we haven't clicked together as a group as often as we'd like." --Field Level Media

item.title: Roubos em museus têm se tornado mais violentos, com ladrões contratados nas redes sociais, diz Europol
item.description: Ladrões de obras de arte na Europa estão cometendo roubos cada vez mais violentos, com foco em ouro e joias, e as quadrilhas especializadas foram substituídas por grupos oportunistas improvisados, recrutados por meio das redes sociais, informou a Europol nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Julia Payne
item.content:encoded: Ladrões de obras de arte na Europa estão cometendo roubos cada vez mais violentos, com foco em ouro e joias, e as quadrilhas especializadas foram substituídas por grupos oportunistas improvisados, recrutados por meio das redes sociais, informou a Europol nesta segunda-feira. O assalto ao Museu do Louvre, em Paris, em outubro do ano passado, foi um exemplo dessas mudanças, disse a Europol, depois que os ladrões ameaçaram guardas e visitantes e roubaram joias no valor de 88 milhões de euros, como a tiara da imperatriz Eugênia. Nos últimos dois anos, os ladrões de obras de arte voltaram sua atenção para metais preciosos, joias e artefatos culturais que oferecem lucros maiores, afirmou a agência de aplicação da lei da UE em um relatório. O preço do ouro subiu 85% nos últimos dois anos, à medida que investidores e bancos centrais recorrem ao metal como um porto seguro. A London Bullion Market Association, que supervisiona o centro de negociação de ouro no mercado de balcão de Londres, alertou que “conforme os preços do ouro atingem níveis históricos, os fluxos ilícitos e as distorções de mercado também estão aumentando”. A Europol afirmou: “os criminosos estão invadindo instalações e vitrines usando ferramentas como marretas, machados, pés-de-cabra e, em alguns casos, explosivos”. Enquanto as quadrilhas tradicionais recorriam ao "engano e à furtividade", contavam com um líder central e possuíam especialização específica, os roubos recentes foram realizados por um grupo descentralizado e improvisado de oportunistas em busca de lucro, recrutados por meio das redes sociais sob o modelo de "crime como serviço", segundo a agência. A Europol acrescentou que os ladrões têm como alvo, cada vez mais, itens de ouro — desde pepitas e moedas até joias. “Metais preciosos podem ser facilmente derretidos, não deixando rastros para as autoridades e facilitando vendas ilícitas durante o processo de receptação. Pedras preciosas em joias, por outro lado, podem ser facilmente removidas e revendidas”, afirmou o relatório. Em janeiro do ano passado, ladrões usaram explosivos para roubar um capacete daciano de ouro de 2.500 anos e três pulseiras de ouro antigas de um museu na Holanda. Os artefatos foram posteriormente recuperados e devolvidos à Romênia, embora uma pulseira ainda esteja desaparecida. A Europol também observou um aumento nos roubos de artefatos de porcelana chinesa antiga, como vasos da dinastia Ming, devido à alta demanda.

item.title: Exportaciones agropecuarias de Argentina crecen 14,9% interanual entre enero y julio
item.description: Las exportaciones del sector agropecuario y agroindustrial crecieron un 14,9% interanual en los primeros siete meses del 2026, a 31.952 millones de dólares, impulsadas principalmente por una expansión de las ventas del maíz y la industria pesquera, dijo el lunes el Consejo Agroindustrial Argentino.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las exportaciones del sector agropecuario y agroindustrial crecieron un 14,9% interanual en los primeros siete meses del 2026, a 31.952 millones de dólares, impulsadas principalmente por una expansión de las ventas del maíz y la industria pesquera, dijo el lunes el Consejo Agroindustrial Argentino. Según el reporte mensual del Consejo (CAA), las exportaciones de maíz de Argentina crecieron un 12% interanual durante este período, a 5.269 millones de dólares, y los embarques del sector pesquero un 18% interanual, a 1.416 millones de dólares. En tanto, concentrando el 33% del total de la participación de las divisas generadas, las exportaciones de soja y su aceite y harina derivados sumaron 10.549 millones de dólares entre enero y julio del 2026, dijo el CAA. Argentina es el mayor exportador mundial de aceite y harina de soja, el tercero de maíz y un importante proveedor de carnes.

item.title: Kremlin diz que ajuda britânica com mísseis à Ucrânia “joga lenha na fogueira”
item.description: O Kremlin disse nesta segunda-feira que a decisão do Reino Unido de fornecer à Ucrânia informações confidenciais sobre componentes de fabricação britânica utilizados na produção dos mísseis de cruzeiro de longo alcance SCALP “jogaria lenha na fogueira” e foi vista por Moscou de forma extremamente negativa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Kremlin disse nesta segunda-feira que a decisão do Reino Unido de fornecer à Ucrânia informações confidenciais sobre componentes de fabricação britânica utilizados na produção dos mísseis de cruzeiro de longo alcance SCALP “jogaria lenha na fogueira” e foi vista por Moscou de forma extremamente negativa. O primeiro-ministro do Reino Unido, Andy Burnham, chegou a Kiev nesta segunda-feira em sua primeira viagem ao exterior desde que assumiu o cargo e deve anunciar o apoio britânico para ajudar Kiev a melhorar sua produção nacional de mísseis de longo alcance. Questionado sobre a visita e o apoio, o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, acusou o Reino Unido de fazer tudo o que pudesse para impedir qualquer avanço rumo a um eventual acordo de paz. “O Reino Unido está envolvido nesta guerra ao lado do regime de Kiev. O Reino Unido, de forma metódica e regular, joga lenha na fogueira e, de forma metódica e regular, trama esquemas para impedir até mesmo o menor progresso no processo de solução pacífica”, disse Peskov aos repórteres. Peskov afirmou que as Forças Armadas russas já estavam coletando dados sistematicamente para identificar a localização de quaisquer instalações de produção de mísseis e, em seguida, destruí-las. Moscou alertou Londres na semana passada sobre “consequências” não especificadas pelo fornecimento de drones a Kiev, acusando o Reino Unido de aprofundar seu envolvimento na guerra após uma reportagem afirmar que drones de fabricação britânica haviam sido usados pela primeira vez em ataques de longo alcance contra a Rússia. Burnham afirmou na ocasião que Londres estava comprometida a apoiar a Ucrânia 100% contra “essa guerra ilegal”. (Reportagem de Dmitry Antonov)

item.title: Strategy earmarks $1.6 billion cash pool for treasury operations, buybacks
item.description: Michael Saylor's Strategy set aside about $1.6 billion in cash to fund future treasury operations, including potential bitcoin purchases and share buybacks, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Saylor's Strategy (MSTR.O) set aside about $1.6 billion in cash to fund future treasury operations, including potential bitcoin purchases and share buybacks, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing on Monday. The world's largest corporate buyer of bitcoin dubbed the liquidity pool "USD Cash," which will be different from a reserve it set up earlier to fund dividends on its preferred stock and interest on its outstanding debt. The new cash pool will have more flexible uses and could be used for bitcoin purchases, share buybacks and other corporate events. It could also give Strategy more flexibility to navigate bitcoin market downturns, allowing it to maintain cash on hand, while continuing to pursue its bitcoin-buying strategy. The move comes after a robust week for bitcoin, which gained a little over 13% in the last five sessions after U.S. President Donald Trump urged Congress to pass legislation establishing clear rules for digital assets. Bitcoin breached the $70,000 mark last week, for the first time since June. Risk assets, like cryptocurrencies, have also benefited after the U.S. Treasury Department's move to double buyback sizes for long-duration debt reined in yields. Higher yields are typically a negative for such assets because they increase the returns on safer investments. Still, bitcoin remains far from the peaks it hit after a staggering run last year.

item.title: Venice adds Gaza documentary by Oscar-winning team to main competition
item.description: A documentary examining Israel's killing of civilians in Gaza was added to the Venice Film Festival line-up on Monday, the second year running that a highly charged work about the conflict has competed for the prestigious Golden Lion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A documentary examining Israel's killing of civilians in Gaza was added to the [USN:L8N43P1IO TEXT:"Venice Film Festival line-up"] on Monday, the second year running that a highly charged work about the conflict has competed for the prestigious Golden Lion. Festival organisers said "NAZA", directed by the Israeli duo Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, will join the main programme for the September 2 to 12 event — the only documentary among this year's 21 contenders. Last year, [USN:L1N3UQ0NW TEXT:""The Voice of Hind Rajab","] which tells the harrowing story of the final hours of [USN:L6N44G0OG TEXT:"a Gazan girl"] trapped in a car under Israeli fire, won second prize at Venice after earning a record 23-minute standing ovation at its premiere. According to a synopsis released by the festival, "NAZA" was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv and "reveals in detail the systems behind Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza". Palestinian health authorities say more than 73,000 people were killed in Gaza after Israel launched its military campaign against the coastal enclave in October 2023 following Hamas's attack on Israel, which killed about 1,200 people, according to Israeli tallies. The Gaza health ministry does not distinguish between civilians and fighters in its count. Israel says its offensive was aimed against Hamas and that it tried to avoid killing civilians, but that the group hid among the civilian population, an assertion that Hamas denies. Abraham and Szor were two of the four co-directors of "No Other Land", which won the Academy Award for best documentary feature in 2025. The film chronicled the destruction of a Palestinian community in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and the relentless expansion of Jewish settlements. "NAZA" was produced by Britain's Guardian newspaper and James Wilson, and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer, the Oscar-winning director of the 2023 Holocaust drama "The Zone of Interest". Wilson and Glazer were also producer and executive producer respectively on "The Voice of Hind Rajab". Israeli authorities last week opened a criminal investigation into the girl's death. "NAZA" will premiere in Venice on September 10. The film joins a high-profile field that includes new works from Martin McDonagh, Florian Zeller, Danny Boyle, Werner Herzog and Hirokazu Kore-eda.

item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah
item.description: A private arbitrator has ordered The Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah with back pay, after the newspaper fired her in September over social media posts about conservative activist Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A private arbitrator has ordered The Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah with back pay, after the newspaper fired her in September over social media posts about conservative activist [USN:L2N3UX0YE TEXT:"Charlie Kirk's assassination"]. The ruling, made public by the Democracy Defenders Fund on Monday, comes as the Post's opinion section faces scrutiny following a push by owner Jeff Bezos to focus on [USN:L2N3PH0XF TEXT:"personal liberties and free markets"]. Here are some more details: Private arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa found the newspaper "did not have good and sufficient cause" to terminate Attiah and had "violated" its labor agreement. "The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct," she wrote. "This decision confirms what we've said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion journalist, and doing that job is not misconduct," said Attiah. A Washington Post spokesperson said the newspaper respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further. The dispute began after Attiah's posts on social media platform Bluesky following Kirk's September 2025 assassination, including one in which she noted Kirk's past comments on Black women. The Post had said in its termination letter that Attiah's posts violated its social media policy, which requires employees' online activity to be respectful and not undermine the integrity of the newspaper's journalism. In February, The Washington Post [USN:L6N3Z015A TEXT:"began layoffs"] impacting a third of its employees, across its international, editing, metro and sports desks amid mounting financial losses. The New York Times first reported the arbitration decision earlier in the day.

item.title: DIHK fürchtet negative Folgen durch eskalierten Handelsstreit in Nordamerika
item.description: Die Wirtschaft fürchtet durch den eskalierten Handelsstreit zwischen den USA und Kanada negative Auswirkungen auf deutsche Unternehmen. Die Deutsche Industrie- und Handelskammer (DIHK) sprach am Montag von einem besorgniserregenden Signal. "Eine weitere Eskalation und Ausweitung der Zölle könnte auch deutsche Unternehmen treffen, die in Nordamerika produzieren und auf eng verzahnte grenzüberschreitende Lieferketten angewiesen sind", sagte DIHK-Handelsexpertin Melanie Vogelbach der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Wirtschaft fürchtet durch den eskalierten Handelsstreit zwischen den USA und Kanada negative Auswirkungen auf deutsche Unternehmen. Die Deutsche Industrie- und Handelskammer (DIHK) sprach am Montag von einem besorgniserregenden Signal. "Eine weitere Eskalation und Ausweitung der Zölle könnte auch deutsche Unternehmen treffen, die in Nordamerika produzieren und auf eng verzahnte grenzüberschreitende Lieferketten angewiesen sind", sagte DIHK-Handelsexpertin Melanie Vogelbach der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Die Handelsgespräche der beiden nordamerikanischen Staaten waren vergangene Woche gescheitert. Beide Seiten gaben sich gegenseitig die Schuld dafür. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte daraufhin Zölle von 50 Prozent auf kanadische Waren im Wert von rund 20 Milliarden Dollar angeordnet, darunter Wein, Möbel, Milchprodukte und Kleidung. Diese gelten ungeachtet des Freihandelsabkommens in Nordamerika, zu dem auch Mexiko gehört. Kanadas Ministerpräsident Mark Carney kündigte am Wochenende Gegenmaßnahmen an. "Man ist im Krieg, wenn man angegriffen wird. Wir wurden angegriffen." Sein Land werde die neuen Zölle Washingtons "Dollar für Dollar" spiegeln. Vogelbach sagte, bei den laufenden Verhandlungen zum nordamerikanischen Freihandelsabkommen USMCA komme es nun umso mehr auf Verlässlichkeit und Berechenbarkeit an. "Neue Handelsbarrieren oder anhaltende Unsicherheit würden das grenzüberschreitende Geschäft erschweren." So könnten Investitionen in die Region gebremst werden.

item.title: Putin hands Russian state right to take control of badly protected infrastructure objects
item.description: President Vladimir Putin on Monday handed the Russian state the authority to take control of critically-important infrastructure facilities if they are deemed to be poorly protected from Ukrainian drone attacks and other threats.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Vladimir Putin on Monday handed the Russian state the authority to take control of critically-important infrastructure facilities if they are deemed to be poorly protected from Ukrainian drone attacks and other threats. The special powers, set out in a presidential decree, will allow the state to take over temporary administration of such facilities at a time when Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on oil refineries and retail warehouses. The state will be able to take control of physical and financial assets and formal ownership rights if the entities responsible for such facilities are judged to have failed in their duty to protect them and are too slow to repair them after any attack, according to the decree. It listed fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transport and logistics facilities and other objects regarded as critically-important for ensuring the security and economic stability of the state and the population as falling within the new decree's scope. Putin last week [USN:L8N44G0XL TEXT:"ordered the government"] to launch a programme to rebuild commercial warehouses damaged or destroyed by Ukraine in recent weeks. Kyiv has attacked at least two dozen warehouses belonging to Russia's top [USN:L1N43K018 TEXT:"online retailer Wildberries"] since July 18, destroying a large chunk of its storage capacity. On Monday, Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon , said four of its logistics hubs in southern Russia had been [USN:L1N44L05J TEXT:"targeted in Ukrainian attacks"].

item.title: Xpeng forecast disappoints as China EV competition heats up
item.description: Chinese EV maker Xpeng forecast third-quarter revenue below Wall Street expectations on Monday, hurt by intensifying competition in the domestic auto market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese EV maker Xpeng (9868.HK) forecast third-quarter revenue below Wall Street expectations on Monday, hurt by intensifying competition in the domestic auto market. The company's U.S.-listed shares fell 3.1% in premarket trading, on course to widen this year's losses of about 40% as of Friday. Here are some details: Xpeng forecast third-quarter revenue between 21.7 billion yuan ($3.23 billion) and 23.4 billion yuan, below analysts' average estimate of 26.61 billion yuan, according to data compiled by LSEG. It delivered 103,295 units in the second quarter ended June 30, within its forecast range of 100,000 to 106,000 units. "During the second quarter of 2026, our operations remained resilient despite industry-wide cost pressures," Xpeng's Vice Chairman and Co-President Hongdi Brian Gu said. Chinese domestic car sales have been [USN:L4N4490F1 TEXT:"in steady decline"] since late last year, as weak consumer demand and years of intense price competition have left the world's biggest auto market glutted with excess capacity, pushing automakers to step up exports and overseas expansion. Xpeng posted second-quarter net loss attributable to ordinary shareholders of 1.34 billion yuan, far higher than estimates of a loss of 511.8 million yuan. It also recalled 264,842 EVs as part of a [USN:L1N44I0AY TEXT:"broader China recall"] involving about 4.3 million vehicles over emergency door-release concerns. Last month, the company launched its MONA L03, AI SUV coupe. Separately, Xpeng's robotics unit raised more than [USN:L1N44L0AQ TEXT:"$900 million"] in its first funding round, setting a record for a single private financing in China's embodied AI sector. ($1 = 6.7227 Chinese yuan renminbi)
